name: Accounting
notes: Competency areas taken from the PA FBLA 2026-2027 Accounting guideline (Accounting - Page 1 of 8, updated August 2026), which lists the same eight knowledge areas as the national event: https://www.pafbla.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/26-27-Accounting-PA.pdf . The national 2025-26 guideline (fbla.org) could not be retrieved (HTTP 403). The PA chart gives weights 0-50 but the bars could not be mapped to individual areas from the text, so question counts are estimated. Event format: 50 minutes, 100 multiple-choice questions. Questions use U.S. GAAP and U.S. tax conventions. Original practice items, not official FBLA test items.

questions.q: Under the accounting equation, which expression is correct?
questions.explain: Assets equal liabilities plus owner equity; the other forms rearrange the terms incorrectly.

questions.q: What is the normal balance of the Unearned Revenue account?
questions.explain: Unearned Revenue is a liability, and liabilities increase with credits.

questions.q: A company pays $1,200 cash for one month of rent already used. Which effect is correct?
choices: Assets fall $1,200 and equity falls $1,200 through rent expense
questions.explain: Cash goes down and an expense reduces equity, so the equation stays balanced.

questions.q: Under the accrual basis of accounting, when are revenues recognized?
choices: When the customer is invoiced at year-end only
At the start of the next fiscal year
When earned, regardless of when cash is received
questions.explain: Accrual accounting records revenue when earned, not when cash moves.

questions.q: A company records a December sale and pays the related sales commission in January. Under the matching principle, when is the commission expense recorded?
choices: December, in the same period as the related sale
The following year, when the contract ends
Never, because it is a cash payment
questions.explain: Expenses are matched to the revenue they helped produce, so the commission falls in December.

questions.q: Which assumption supports reporting long-term equipment at historical cost less accumulated depreciation rather than at liquidation value?
questions.explain: The going concern assumption says the business will keep operating, so asset values are not forced to liquidation values.

questions.q: A $40 office supply purchase is expensed immediately rather than capitalized. Which concept best justifies this?
questions.explain: Immaterial amounts may be expensed for convenience without affecting decisions.

questions.q: A trial balance has total debits of $85,400 and total credits of $85,400. Which conclusion is correct?
choices: Equal totals prove all transactions were recorded correctly
The balance sheet must be out of balance
Totals must equal zero to be valid
Equal totals do not prove every entry is correct, since some errors leave the totals balanced
questions.explain: A trial balance catches some errors, but omitted entries and wrong-account postings still balance.

questions.q: Which account is a contra-asset?
questions.explain: A contra-asset reduces a related asset account and carries a credit balance.

questions.q: Land is bought for $300,000, with a $25,000 title search and a $5,000 legal fee to acquire it. What is the recorded cost of the land under U.S. GAAP?
questions.explain: All costs necessary to get the land ready for use are capitalized: $300,000 + $25,000 + $5,000 = $330,000.

questions.q: Which document is the best source for recording a credit sale?
questions.explain: The sales invoice documents the sale and the amount owed on account.

questions.q: A sole proprietor owns a home that is not used in the business. Under the economic entity assumption, how is the home treated in the business accounts?
choices: Recorded as a liability of the business
questions.explain: Personal assets are kept separate from the business entity.

questions.q: At year-end, employees have earned $6,000 of wages that are unpaid. Which adjusting entry is needed?
choices: Debit Wages Expense $6,000; credit Wages Payable $6,000
questions.explain: The expense belongs to this period and the unpaid amount is a liability.

questions.q: A 12-month insurance premium is paid in advance. Which treatment is correct under accrual accounting?
choices: Expense the full premium at payment
Record a prepaid asset at payment and expense one-twelfth each month
Record revenue when the premium is paid
Defer the premium until the policy expires
questions.explain: The prepaid asset is consumed monthly as coverage is used.

questions.q: Which body establishes U.S. GAAP for private and public companies?
questions.explain: The FASB issues the Accounting Standards Codification that forms U.S. GAAP.

questions.q: Which federal law created the SEC and set up periodic reporting by companies with registered securities?
questions.explain: The 1933 Act governs initial registration; the 1934 Act created the SEC and ongoing reporting.

questions.q: Under Sarbanes-Oxley, which officers must certify the accuracy of periodic financial reports?
questions.explain: SOX Section 302 requires the CEO and CFO to certify periodic reports.

questions.q: Which professional body issues the Code of Professional Conduct for U.S. CPAs?
questions.explain: The AICPA sets ethical standards for its CPA members.

questions.q: Which body was created by Sarbanes-Oxley to oversee audits of public companies?
questions.explain: The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board was created by SOX in 2002.

questions.q: Which statement about inventory costing is accurate?
choices: IFRS permits LIFO, while U.S. GAAP prohibits it
Both U.S. GAAP and IFRS permit LIFO
Neither U.S. GAAP nor IFRS permits FIFO
U.S. GAAP permits LIFO, while IFRS prohibits it
questions.explain: LIFO is allowed under U.S. GAAP but not under IFRS, a common exam comparison.

questions.q: Which principle requires a company to use the same accounting methods from period to period unless a change is disclosed?
questions.explain: Consistency makes statements comparable across periods.

questions.q: Which statement reflects a core independence requirement for auditors?
choices: Auditors may take contingent fees on all attest work
Auditors must be independent in fact and in appearance
Client confidentiality may be breached for personal gain
Objectivity applies only to internal accountants
questions.explain: Auditors must be independent in fact and appearance to keep the opinion credible.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an external audit opinion?
choices: To guarantee the company will remain solvent
To determine the company's income tax liability
To give reasonable assurance that statements are free of material misstatement and fairly presented under GAAP
To set the next year's operating budget
questions.explain: An audit gives reasonable, not absolute, assurance about the financial statements.

questions.q: Which Sarbanes-Oxley section requires management to assess and report on the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting?
questions.explain: Section 404 covers management assessment of internal control; 302 covers officer certification.

questions.q: Which SEC form is the annual report that public U.S. companies file with audited financial statements?
questions.explain: The 10-K is the annual report; 10-Q is quarterly and 8-K reports events.

questions.q: A CPA finds a material error in a client financial statement. What does professional ethics require?
choices: Delay disclosure until the next audit
Not knowingly associate with materially false statements and seek correction
Issue an unqualified opinion to avoid conflict
Wait for a regulator to find the error first
questions.explain: A CPA must not knowingly be associated with false financial information.

questions.q: Which book records transactions in chronological order before they are posted to the ledger?
questions.explain: The journal is the book of original entry; the ledger holds the posted account balances.

questions.q: The owner invests $20,000 cash in the business. Which journal entry is correct?
questions.explain: Cash increases (debit) and owner equity increases (credit).

questions.q: A business buys $3,500 of supplies on account. Which entry is correct?
questions.explain: Supplies are an asset until used, and the unpaid bill is a liability.

questions.q: Which account is closed directly to Retained Earnings at year-end, rather than through Income Summary?
questions.explain: Dividends are not revenue or expense, so they close straight to Retained Earnings.

questions.q: A bank statement shows $12,400. Deposits in transit total $1,800 and outstanding checks total $2,300. What is the adjusted bank balance?
A customer pays $900 on account. Which entry is correct?
questions.explain: Collecting a receivable increases cash and reduces the receivable.

questions.q: Equipment costing $60,000 has a 5-year life, no salvage value, and straight-line depreciation. What is annual depreciation expense?
questions.explain: $60,000 divided by 5 years equals $12,000 per year.

questions.q: The same equipment (cost $60,000, 5-year life, straight-line, no salvage) has been depreciated for two full years. What is its net book value?
questions.explain: Accumulated depreciation is $24,000, so $60,000 less $24,000 leaves $36,000.

questions.q: A company receives $3,600 in advance for 12 months of service beginning October 1. How much revenue is earned by December 31?
questions.explain: Three of the twelve months have passed: $3,600 times 3/12 is $900.

questions.q: Beginning inventory is $15,000, purchases are $62,000, and ending inventory is $18,000. What is cost of goods sold?
A prepaid rent asset has been partly used up. Which adjusting entry is needed for the used portion?
choices: Debit Rent Expense; credit Prepaid Rent for the portion used
Debit Prepaid Rent; credit Rent Expense
Debit Rent Payable; credit Prepaid Rent
questions.explain: The used portion moves from an asset to an expense.

questions.q: A $450 utility payment was recorded as $540 (debit Utilities Expense, credit Cash). Which correcting entry is needed?
questions.explain: Expense was overstated by $90, so reverse that excess: cash and expense each reduced.

questions.q: In the usual order of preparation, which financial statement is prepared first?
questions.explain: Net income from the income statement feeds the retained earnings statement and balance sheet.

questions.q: Which account will appear on the post-closing trial balance?
questions.explain: Only permanent (balance sheet) accounts remain after closing.

questions.q: Merchandise that cost $1,400 is sold. Which entry records the cost of goods sold under the perpetual inventory system?
choices: Debit Cost of Goods Sold $1,400; credit Merchandise Inventory $1,400
Debit Merchandise Inventory $1,400; credit Cost of Goods Sold $1,400
Debit Sales $1,400; credit Cost of Goods Sold $1,400
Debit Cost of Goods Sold $1,400; credit Accounts Payable $1,400
questions.explain: The cost leaves inventory and becomes an expense at the time of sale.

questions.q: A company has revenues of $90,000 and expenses of $72,000 for the year. What does the closing entry do to Retained Earnings?
questions.explain: Net income of $18,000 increases Retained Earnings with a credit.

questions.q: A $50,000 note bears 6% annual interest, and four months of interest is unpaid at year-end. What is the accrued interest?
questions.explain: $50,000 times 6% times 4/12 equals $1,000.

questions.q: Accounts receivable are $200,000. The allowance has a $1,500 credit balance before adjustment, and $9,000 is estimated uncollectible. What is bad debt expense?
questions.explain: The allowance must go from $1,500 to $9,000, so $7,500 is expensed.

questions.q: A $10,000 credit sale has terms 2/10, n/30, and the customer pays within the discount period. What cash is received?
questions.explain: A 2% discount on $10,000 is $200, leaving $9,800.

questions.q: Which account is debited when equipment is purchased for cash?
questions.explain: The asset increases by debit; cash is the account credited.

questions.q: Under the allowance method, which entry records estimated bad debts at year-end?
choices: Debit Accounts Receivable; credit Bad Debt Expense
Debit Cash; credit Bad Debt Expense
Debit Bad Debt Expense; credit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts
Debit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts; credit Cash
questions.explain: The estimate is expensed in the same period as the sale, with a contra-asset credit.

questions.q: Which of the following is a current liability?
questions.explain: Current liabilities are due within one year or the operating cycle.

questions.q: Which best describes the aging of accounts receivable method?
choices: Estimates bad debts based on the age of each receivable balance
Estimates bad debts as a percentage of credit sales
Writes off accounts only when a customer declares bankruptcy
Records bad debts only when cash is collected
questions.explain: Older balances are assumed to be less collectible, so a higher percentage is applied to them.

questions.q: Under the direct write-off method, which statement is true?
choices: Expenses are matched to revenue of the same period
Bad debts are expensed when a specific account is deemed uncollectible
An allowance account is always required
Receivables are reported at net realizable value
questions.explain: Direct write-off is simple but does not match expense to revenue, so it is not GAAP for most companies.

questions.q: A $12,000, six-month note bears 8% annual interest. What interest is due at maturity?
questions.explain: $12,000 times 8% times 6/12 equals $480.

questions.q: Merchandise costs $5,000 on terms 2/10, n/30. Under the net method, the bill is paid within the discount period. What cash is paid?
questions.explain: Under the net method the purchase is recorded net of the 2% discount: $5,000 less $100.

questions.q: Net credit sales are $600,000 and average accounts receivable are $75,000. What is receivables turnover?
questions.explain: $600,000 divided by $75,000 equals 8.0 times.

questions.q: Receivables turnover is 8.0 times on a 365-day year. What is the average collection period?
questions.explain: 365 divided by 8.0 is about 45.6 days.

questions.q: Which document confirms that goods received match the purchase order before a vendor invoice is paid?
questions.explain: The receiving report is part of the three-way match used before payment.

questions.q: A customer returns goods for $300 credit on account. Which entry is correct?
choices: Debit Accounts Receivable $300; credit Sales Returns and Allowances $300
Debit Cash $300; credit Sales Returns and Allowances $300
Debit Sales Returns and Allowances $300; credit Cash $300
Debit Sales Returns and Allowances $300; credit Accounts Receivable $300
questions.explain: Returns reduce sales and reduce the amount the customer owes.

questions.q: The allowance has a $2,000 debit balance before adjustment, and an $11,000 credit balance is needed. What is bad debt expense?
questions.explain: The adjustment must move the allowance by $13,000 from a debit to a $11,000 credit.

questions.q: Under the allowance method, a $800 receivable is written off against the allowance. What is the effect on net realizable value?
questions.explain: The write-off reduces both gross receivables and the allowance by the same amount.

questions.q: What is a trade discount?
choices: A reduction for early payment, recorded as a sales discount
A reduction from list price offered to a class of buyers, not recorded in the accounts
Interest charged on a late payment
questions.explain: Trade discounts are netted into the price and never appear as separate accounts.

questions.q: Accounts payable are $48,000 before $6,000 of invoices for goods received before year-end are recorded. What should accounts payable be?
questions.explain: Unrecorded liabilities for goods received before year-end must be accrued.

questions.q: Which of the following is a current asset?
questions.explain: Receivables due within a year or the operating cycle are current assets.

questions.q: Accounts receivable total $150,000 and the allowance is $12,000. What is net realizable value?
Which form does a sole proprietor use to report business income and expenses?
questions.explain: Sole proprietors report business profit or loss on Schedule C attached to the personal return.

questions.q: Which form is the quarterly federal return reporting income tax withheld and FICA taxes?
questions.explain: Form 941 is the employer quarterly return; W-2 is annual and 940 is for FUTA.

questions.q: Which federal return does a C corporation file?
questions.explain: C corporations file Form 1120; partnerships file 1065 and S corporations file 1120-S.

questions.q: Which payroll tax does the employer pay that matches the employee Social Security and Medicare contribution?
questions.explain: Employers match the employee share of FICA.

questions.q: Which form reports each employee annual wages and tax withholdings?
questions.explain: The W-2 is issued to each employee and filed with the Social Security Administration.

questions.q: Straight-line book depreciation differs from MACRS tax depreciation. How is this difference classified in the accounts?
choices: Permanent difference that is never reversed
No difference, since both methods total the same
Temporary difference that creates a deferred tax liability
questions.explain: Accelerated tax depreciation early on creates a deferred tax liability that reverses over time.

questions.q: A store sells $800 of merchandise subject to 7% sales tax. What total does the customer pay?
questions.explain: $800 times 1.07 equals $856.

questions.q: An employee earns $2,000 gross wages. Only the 7.65% employee FICA tax is withheld. What is net pay after FICA?
Under IRS rules, which describes an ordinary and necessary business expense?
choices: A personal vacation paid by the business
A political contribution, which is always deductible
An expense that is common and accepted in the trade and helpful to the business
questions.explain: Ordinary means common in the trade and necessary means helpful and appropriate.

questions.q: Under current U.S. federal tax rules, business meal expenses are generally deductible at what percentage?
questions.explain: The general rule for business meals is 50 percent deductibility.

questions.q: Which statement reports revenues and expenses for a period?
questions.explain: The income statement reports net income for a period of time.

questions.q: Which balance sheet section lists assets expected to be converted to cash within one year or the operating cycle?
questions.explain: Current assets are listed first and are expected to turn into cash within a year.

questions.q: Which cash flow is an operating activity under U.S. GAAP?
questions.explain: Operating activities relate to cash from normal business operations.

questions.q: Which item is an investing activity?
questions.explain: Buying long-term assets is investing; loan principal is financing and interest is operating.

questions.q: Sales are $420,000, cost of goods sold is $252,000, and operating expenses are $98,000. What is the gross profit margin?
questions.explain: Gross profit is $168,000, and $168,000 divided by $420,000 is 40%.

questions.q: Current assets are $180,000 and current liabilities are $120,000. What is the current ratio?
Current assets are $180,000, including $60,000 of inventory. Current liabilities are $120,000. What is the quick ratio?
questions.explain: Quick assets are $120,000, and $120,000 divided by $120,000 is 1.0.

questions.q: Total liabilities are $400,000 and total equity is $500,000. What is the debt-to-equity ratio?
Net income is $75,000 and average total assets are $1,200,000. What is return on assets?
Net income is $75,000 and average stockholders equity is $500,000. What is return on equity?
Which statement reports assets, liabilities, and equity at a single point in time?
questions.explain: The balance sheet is a snapshot as of a date.

questions.q: Net income is $300,000, preferred dividends are $30,000, and 90,000 weighted average common shares are outstanding. What is basic EPS?
questions.explain: Earnings available to common ($270,000) divided by 90,000 shares is $3.00.

questions.q: Which items are typically reconciled in the statement of changes in stockholders equity?
questions.explain: Equity changes come from net income, dividends, and stock transactions.

questions.q: Which relationship describes the statement of retained earnings?
choices: Beginning retained earnings - net income + dividends = ending retained earnings
Beginning retained earnings + net income - dividends = ending retained earnings
Net income - beginning retained earnings = ending retained earnings
Beginning retained earnings + dividends - net income = ending retained earnings
questions.explain: Net income increases retained earnings and dividends reduce it.

questions.q: Beginning retained earnings are $220,000, net income is $64,000, and dividends are $20,000. What is ending retained earnings?
Cost of goods sold is $450,000 and average inventory is $90,000. What is inventory turnover?
questions.explain: $450,000 divided by $90,000 is 5.0 times.

questions.q: EBIT is $360,000 and interest expense is $60,000. What is times interest earned?
questions.explain: $360,000 divided by $60,000 is 6.0 times.

questions.q: Under the indirect method, which non-cash item is added back to net income in operating activities?
questions.explain: Depreciation reduces net income but does not use cash, so it is added back.

questions.q: Which software feature lets a transaction entered in one module update the general ledger automatically?
questions.explain: Integrated modules share data so one entry flows through to the ledger.

questions.q: Which technology control limits access to accounting data to authorized users based on job duties?
questions.explain: Role-based access restricts users to the functions their job needs.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of an ERP system in accounting?
choices: Integrating business processes and data into one system
questions.explain: ERP systems connect finance, sales, purchasing, and inventory in one database.

questions.q: Which process checks that entered data meets defined rules and is accurate before it is processed?
questions.explain: Validation rules catch errors such as invalid account numbers at entry.

questions.q: What is XBRL primarily used for?
choices: Tagging financial data so computers can read and compare it
questions.explain: XBRL tags financial statement data in a standard machine-readable format.

questions.q: Which control best reduces the risk of duplicate or unauthorized vendor payments?
choices: Approving invoices without comparing them to receiving records
Three-way match of purchase order, receiving report, and vendor invoice
questions.explain: The three-way match confirms the bill is for goods ordered and received before payment.

questions.q: Which credential is awarded to accountants who pass the Uniform CPA Examination and meet state licensing requirements?
questions.explain: The Certified Public Accountant credential requires the CPA exam and state licensure.

questions.q: Which certification focuses on management accounting and internal financial decision support?
questions.explain: The Certified Management Accountant credential focuses on management accounting.

questions.q: Which career is most closely associated with evaluating internal controls within an organization?
questions.explain: Internal auditors test controls and report on risk within the organization.

questions.q: What does an Enrolled Agent credential allow a person to do?
questions.explain: Enrolled Agents are federally licensed to represent taxpayers before the IRS.

vocab.def: Assets equal liabilities plus owner equity, and every transaction keeps the equation balanced.
Revenue is recorded when earned and expenses when incurred, regardless of when cash moves.
Expenses are recorded in the same period as the revenues they helped generate.
The assumption that a business will continue operating long enough to use its assets and meet its obligations.
An item is material if omitting or misstating it could influence the decisions of users of the statements.
Assets are recorded at their original cost, including costs necessary to get them ready for use.
Business transactions are kept separate from the personal transactions of owners.
An account that offsets a related account and reduces its reported balance, such as accumulated depreciation.
Generally accepted accounting principles, the framework of standards used to prepare U.S. financial statements.
The Financial Accounting Standards Board, the private body that sets U.S. GAAP.
The Securities and Exchange Commission, which regulates public securities and requires periodic reports from public companies.
A 2002 federal law that strengthened corporate governance, auditor independence, and internal control requirements.
The Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, created by SOX to oversee audits of public companies.
The ethics rules that govern the professional conduct of certified public accountants.
The requirement that an auditor be free of relationships that could impair objectivity, in fact and in appearance.
The book of original entry where transactions are first recorded in chronological order.
The collection of all accounts that holds the posted balances used to prepare statements.
A list of all ledger account balances used to check that total debits equal total credits.
A journal entry made at period end to record revenues and expenses not yet recorded in the accounts.
Entries made at year-end that move temporary account balances to Retained Earnings.
An expense incurred in the period but not yet paid, recorded as a liability.
Cash received before goods or services are delivered, recorded as a liability until earned.
A process that explains the difference between the bank balance and the book cash balance.
The systematic allocation of a tangible asset cost over its useful life.
Amounts customers owe the business for credit sales, usually current assets.
A contra-asset account that holds the estimated amount of receivables that will not be collected.
A method that estimates uncollectible accounts in the period of sale, matching bad debt expense to revenue.
A method that expenses a bad debt only when a specific account is deemed uncollectible.
A method that estimates uncollectible accounts by applying higher loss rates to older receivable balances.
A reduction from list price offered to a class of buyers, which is not recorded in the accounts.
A reduction offered for early payment, such as 2/10, n/30, recorded when the discount is taken.
A document confirming the quantity and condition of goods received, used in the three-way match.
The IRS form attached to Form 1040 on which a sole proprietor reports business income and expenses.
The U.S. federal income tax return filed by C corporations.
The quarterly federal payroll return reporting income tax withheld and FICA taxes.
The annual statement reporting each employee wages and tax withholdings.
The Social Security and Medicare payroll taxes paid by both employees and employers.
A future tax obligation created when taxable income will exceed book income in later periods.
A business expense that is common in the trade and helpful and appropriate for the business.
A financial statement that reports revenues, expenses, and net income for a period.
A financial statement that reports assets, liabilities, and equity at a specific date.
A statement that reports cash inflows and outflows from operating, investing, and financing activities.
A statement that reconciles beginning retained earnings with net income and dividends to get ending balance.
Current assets divided by current liabilities, a measure of short-term liquidity.
Cash, marketable securities, and receivables divided by current liabilities, excluding inventory and prepaids.
Net income divided by average stockholders equity, a measure of profitability for owners.
Net income available to common shareholders divided by weighted average common shares outstanding.
A way to present operating cash flow by starting with net income and adjusting for non-cash items and working capital changes.
Enterprise resource planning software that integrates finance, sales, purchasing, and other processes in one database.
A security control that restricts system access to the functions each user needs for their job.
Rules that check entered data for accuracy and completeness before it is processed.
Extensible Business Reporting Language, a standard for tagging financial data so computers can read it.
A control comparing the purchase order, receiving report, and vendor invoice before payment.
A control that separates authorization, recording, and custody so no single person controls a full transaction.
Certified Public Accountant, a license earned by passing the Uniform CPA Examination and meeting state requirements.
Certified Management Accountant, a credential focused on management accounting and financial decision support.
Certified Internal Auditor, a credential for professionals who audit and assess controls and risk within organizations.
Certified Financial Planner, a credential for professionals who advise individuals on personal financial planning.
A federally licensed tax practitioner authorized to represent taxpayers before the IRS.
A professional who evaluates an organization controls, governance, and risk management processes.
